html:
The global geopolitical landscape is significantly impacted by the intensifying US-Iran conflict, with US forces concluding their two-decade presence in Iraq and Donald Trump offering conflicting signals on a resolution. US forces' withdrawal from Iraq on Wednesday, completing a pullout agreed under former president Joe Biden, raises fears of a security vacuum and emboldened Iran-backed militias.

US-Iran Tensions: Donald Trump has warned of possible new strikes on Iran, stating that the Iran conflict would conclude 'very soon,' but offered no specific details. Simultaneously, Trump rejected Iran's offer to pause fighting and a truce offer, with oil prices spiking following this rejection. US and Iran continue to trade barbs, with Araghchi vowing a 'doomsday war' but remaining open to diplomacy. Iran is leveraging the Strait of Hormuz, where a vessel was struck by an unknown projectile, and stated readiness for preemptive strikes if threatened. Five men arrested near a UK air base used by U.S. bombers in the Iran war are being investigated for a possible Iran link, while Russia advised Washington to focus on peaceful resolutions with Tehran.

Great Power Dynamics & AI: Beyond the Middle East, Donald Trump discussed AI development with tech bosses at the White House, where a voluntary accord on safety controls was signed. However, Trump stated he didn't want to work with Chinese President Xi Jinping on AI oversight, following a revelation that a Chinese AI tool could describe how to make bioweapons. Potential Taiwan tension also prompted a 'last minute' change in a Trump-Xi National Archives visit. Meanwhile, Beijing warns of retaliation if Europe imposes curbs on Chinese businesses. In Eastern Europe, Ukraine's prized steel industry has been left in ruins by a Russian missile campaign, with missile alerts costing Ukraine an estimated $45m for every hour they halt businesses. North Korea has recently completed two road bridges, easing transport to strategic allies Russia and China.

Middle East Conflicts: The Israeli-Palestinian conflict continues to see violence, with a Palestinian child killed and another girl severely injured by Israeli strikes in Gaza. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers clashed with security forces, stopping them from returning a Palestinian family to their home, a situation Donald Trump blamed on a 'handful of rioters.' Jordan condemned the storming of Al-Aqsa Mosque by an Israeli far-right minister and settlers. Smotrich called for a West Bank war and the annexation of Lebanon and Gaza, a stance rejected by Qatar. Washington is pushing for Hezbollah disarmament in Lebanon, with a secret document reportedly containing a proposal to Trump on how to eliminate Hezbollah. Morocco experienced protests over deepening ties with Israel, even as Emirati social media users celebrated the UAE's delegation remaining for Benjamin Netanyahu's UN speech.

Global Economy & Technology: Australia's inflation leaped to 4% in the year to August, stoking fears of a fifth interest rate hike before Christmas, with Jim Chalmers citing 'higher global oil prices.' Mideast crude oil flows have hit 98% of pre-war levels, while Iran's rial reached a record low amid persistent economic and military pressures. Iraq has begun importing gasoline via Syria to circumvent potential disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz. In the tech sector, OpenAI decided not to release its new AI model, GPT-6.1 Astra, citing safety concerns and a failure to meet required standards.

Broader Developments: The UK government's online safety crackdown is progressing, with Culture secretary Lisa Nandy indicating that banning under-16s from social media platforms is only a 'staging post.' Andy Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour's annual party conference. France's National Rally denied fresh antisemitism claims. Hungary's reckoning with Orban's corrupt system picked up speed with high-profile arrests. Morocco's king appointed the country’s first woman prime minister. Environmentally, a government building collapsed into a river in Nepal amid floods, and heatwaves and wildfires exposed a third of the world's population to "extremely poor" ozone air quality in the first eight months of 2026. Scientists also identified a new species of penguin, the first in over a century.
